headline: Record volumes lift revenue, losses widen, outlook raised
summary_short: Natera's Q1 2026 revenue rose 38.8% y/y to $696.6M on record test volumes (1.01M processed, oncology +54.4%), while the GAAP net loss widened to $85.1M ($0.60/share); management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.74B-$2.82B from $2.62B-$2.70B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 38.8% y/y to $696.6M as processed test volume rose 18.5% to over 1 million units for the first time, with oncology volume up 54.4%. Gross margin expanded to 64.7% from 63.1% on higher ASPs and lower per-test costs. Total opex (R&D + SG&A) rose 36.0% y/y to $538.6M on headcount growth and clinical-trial spend, widening the operating loss to $93.5M and net loss to $85.1M ($0.60/share) from $66.9M ($0.50/share). Cash was $1,087.9M, up from $1,076.1M at year-end on ~$11.8M of positive net cash inflow. Natera raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.74B-$2.82B (from $2.62B-$2.70B) and gross-margin guidance to ~64%-66%, raised R&D guidance to $800M-$900M, and held SG&A guidance unchanged at $1.125B-$1.225B.

drivers.explanation: Release frames Q1 as a record quarter — first time topping 1M processed tests, record oncology unit growth — prompting a raised full-year revenue, margin and R&D outlook.
Growth attributed to an increase in volume (test volume +18.5% y/y, oncology +54.4%) plus average selling price improvements.
Higher gross margin (64.7% vs 63.1%) attributed to higher revenues and continued progress reducing cost of revenues associated with tests processed.
Total opex rose $142.7M y/y (+36.0%) to $538.6M on headcount growth for new product offerings and higher clinical trial expenses, outpacing the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain.
Net loss widened as the $142.7M y/y opex increase exceeded the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain; $5.7M of new intangible-amortization expense (none in Q1 2025) also weighed on the total.
Cash, equivalents and restricted cash rose to $1,087.9M from $1,076.1M at year-end on $40.2M operating cash flow and $3.7M financing inflow, partly offset by $32.1M of investing outflow.
